attributes.probed_form: THE REPAIR TABLE, verbatim. EIGHT by unique prefix, i.e. a missing version suffix, each taking the extractor's own `did_you_mean`: `attempt.fn80011bbc-matchindex-coalesce` -> `.20260831.v1`; `claim.law.webfrank-cfg-entry-pseudotarget-false-negative` -> `.20260831.v1`; `claim.law.C1_permute-recolor-composition-needs-a-permutation-legal-in-our-colouring` -> `.20260901.v1`; `claim.law.DC` -> `claim.law.DC_copy-form-class-is-directional-and-its-inverse-population-is-unserved.20260901.v1`; `attempt.pbprojcalc-zero-web-schedule` -> `.20260831.v2`; `claim.law.HV_emb-sda21-relocation-offset-differs-between-our-objects-and-the-target` -> `.20260901.v1`; `claim.law.webfrank-permutation-is-audited-in-our-colouring` -> `.20260831.v1`. TWO AMBIGUOUS, resolved by reading the citing sentence rather than by picking a candidate: movieplayer::fn_800D8F28's `claim.LZ` (2 candidates) -> `claim.LZ_copy-form-taxonomy-and-payoff-inversion.20260901.v1`, because the citing sentence is 'the wall claim.law.DC and claim.LZ both recorded as needing a v2 combined pass' and that record is the one carrying 'THE v2 REQUIREMENT ... what v2 needs is a combined pass that applies the renaming and the form rewrite together', while the sibling claim.LZ_webfrank-equivalent-copy-form-edit-class.20260901.v1 contains neither string. camera::camera_mode_level's `attempt.CN` (5 candidates) -> `attempt.CN_camera-mode-level-cluster-a-readiness.20260901.v1`, because the citing sentence is 'attempt.CN concluded the remainder is not a bijective renaming either ... from a refusal at +0x8b8', a finding about THAT function, and it is the only CN record about camera_mode_level. THE SUBSTITUTION IS GUARDED: the pattern is `re.escape(short) + r'(?![A-Za-z0-9_-])(?!\.\d)'`, so a short id that is a PREFIX of the correct id already spelled elsewhere in the same prose is never double-suffixed, every replacement id is checked to resolve against memory_graph/records BEFORE any write, and a short form that does not appear on its pin's mechanism line aborts the whole run rather than editing the wrong line -- which is how the tenth defect was found.
attributes.residual: TWO CORRECTIONS TO THE HANDOFF, both measured, and the second is the one that would have cost a later lane real time. (1) THE COUNT IS 10, NOT 13, AND THE THREE MISSING ONES ARE ALREADY FIXED IN CODE. T24's record says '13 dangling citations remain in config/GUNE5D/webfrank.json (3 trailing-period law ids, 10 version-suffix-short ids of which 8 resolve uniquely by prefix, now reported as unresolved_citations with did_you_mean)'. That sentence merges two different lists produced by two different code paths. `unresolved_citations` (built from `cites_records`) reports the 10; the 3 trailing-period ids were only ever visible to the LAW-BACKED classifier's `named` set, and T24's own hardening in the same run -- requiring the backing law to resolve -- already handles them. Swept live this run, `provenance_laws_unresolved` is EMPTY across every pinned TU, and the three pins T24 names (atree::DoAnimateTreeFrame, gcontrolpads::G3DReadControlPadStates, btext::FindStringMessageListSub_8001FC4C) each cite `claim.law.live-zero-copy-vs-remat-is-allocator-not-source.20260831.v1` followed by an ordinary SENTENCE-ENDING period, which `_mechanism_citations` strips correctly. There was nothing left to repair there, and a lane taking the 13 literally would have hunted three non-defects. A naive regex confirms why the shape is a trap: matching an id token followed by an optional period finds EIGHTEEN such occurrences across the file, of which the 3 T24 named are indistinguishable from the other 15 -- the difference was never in the prose, it was in which classifier happened to look. (2) ONE `did_you_mean` IS WRONG, AND FOLLOWING IT WOULD HAVE MISCITED A RECORD. worldcol::CTriListCollide's row reports cited=`claim.CN`, candidates=1, did_you_mean=`claim.CN_census-rerun-canary-validated-filter.20260901.v1`. That is not a truncated id: the prose writes the GLOB `claim.CN_*` ('claim.CN_* left this function open as one of three with 9-20 atom windows'), and `_mechanism_citations` tokenizes it as bare `claim.CN` because `*` is not an identifier character. The suggestion is doubly wrong -- that id is ALREADY cited correctly two sentences earlier for a DIFFERENT finding, and the sentence carrying the glob attributes 'beyond the 8-atom exhaustive search bound', which greps to exactly one record in the corpus: `attempt.CN_census-rerun-four-closures.20260901.v1`, an `attempt.`, not a `claim.`. So the glob was repaired to that id instead. GENERAL RULE FOR THE NEXT REPAIRER: a `did_you_mean` with candidates=1 is a PREFIX FACT, not a resolution -- it says one accepted id extends the cited string, which is also true of every abbreviation and every glob. Read the citing sentence before accepting any of them, and treat a suggestion naming an id the same pin already cites as a signal that the token is not a truncation at all.

hypothesis.cheapest_refuting_observation: Zero builds: re-run the sweep in this record's verification (`_pin_provenance` over every unit in webfrank.json) at any later commit. If it still reports only this run's three forward references once they are accepted, the surface is not re-rotting and the test is not worth its maintenance. If the count has grown, the test pays for itself immediately. The measurement is the same one either way, which is what makes it a fair test of the hypothesis rather than an argument for it.
hypothesis.count_consequence: None: no instruction count in the image can change, because no rule stage, hash or source byte was touched. The `git diff --numstat` of 9 lines against 10 repairs is the whole footprint, and the unchanged `Postprocessor split` line is the check that it stayed prose.
hypothesis.screened_against_target: no — this is a config/corpus-hygiene item and touches no compiled byte, so there is no target assembly to screen against. What WAS screened, and is the equivalent obligation: the build output before and after is identical (same split line, same `main.dol: OK`), so the repair is provably prose-only.
hypothesis.statement: The citation surface will re-rot, because nothing prevents it: 154-plus pins carry free prose, ids are typed by hand into it, and the only reader that checks them is a report nobody is required to run. The cheap durable fix is a TEST, not another repair pass -- assert in tools/gdl/tests that every `(claim|attempt)\.` token in every webfrank.json `mechanism` resolves to a record under memory_graph/records, with an explicit allowlist for the two idioms the corpus deliberately uses (`DEAD-ID[...]`, which the extractor already understands, and the `<family>_*` glob, which it does not).
